extracted.intended_audience: UKRI applicants, assessors (reviewers and panellists), UKRI staff and funding administrators
extracted.subtask_description: High-level policy setting eight principles that must govern assessment and decision-making for all UKRI competitive funding opportunities, describing expectations for assessors, panels, transparency, impartiality, confidentiality, integrity, equality and separation of duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectively, assessors should have the appropriate knowledge and expertise to assess the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will ensure that all reviewers have appropriate knowledge, expertise or experience in the relevant field to review an application; use a diverse range of experts to provide assessments; appoint panellists who have the appropriate range of expertise, experience and knowledge to carry out assessments, which includes expertise for cross-disciplinary applications; provide clear, tailored funding opportunity guidance to all assessors before they undertake review of applications. Panellists will be provided with additional materials to ensure they can carry out an appropriate assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When a funding opportunity is advertised, UKRI must ensure the following are made available and accessible to all users and the public: the approach for the assessment of the application, the assessment criteria, information on how funding outcomes are communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will publish guidelines, the assessment criteria and details of the assessment process for all funding opportunities prior to the submission of applications. Where appropriate and where the assessment approach allows, applicants will be given an opportunity to see and respond to anonymised reviewer comments. UKRI will inform applicants of the outcome within a reasonable timeframe after the final decision; ensure feedback is provided relevant to the assessment approaches used within a reasonable timeframe; publish names of panellists within a reasonable timeframe after decisions; normally keep reviewer identities anonymous to applicants (but may publish reviewer-related information such as Peer Review College membership or aggregate data); publish outcomes of applications within a reasonable timeframe and provide details of funded applications in a searchable public website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment of applications must be fair, and sources of biases should be recognised and mitigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will ensure all assessors are informed on safeguarding the decision-making process and the importance of making fair and objective decisions before panel assessments; provide guidance to office administrators and panellists to promote fairness and objectivity; have processes to identify and manage reviewer, panellist and staff conflicts of interest (managed in line with UKRI's declaration of interest policy); provide guidance to applicants, reviewers and panellists to help them determine if they are conflicted; provide guidance on ways to manage conflicts of interest and expected conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment of applications must use a process that considers both the aims and objectives of the funding opportunity, and the time and resource required to provide the most appropriate approach to enable the best funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will use a set of tools enabling an assessment approach appropriate for the complexity and funding level of the proposed opportunity; ensure information and data required to support effective assessment, funding decision and post-decision management are collected appropriately and at the appropriate time. UKRI supports DORA and recognises the relationship between research assessment and research integrity; will not use journal-based metrics (such as journal impact factors) as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual researcher’s contributions, or to make funding decisions. In alignment with CoARA, UKRI recognises the diversity of contributions to, and careers in, research according to the needs and nature of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality in the assessment process must be maintained to protect the applicant’s ideas, intellectual properties, confidential, commercially sensitive and personal data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will instruct individuals and organisations involved in assessment to treat in confidence all applications and related data (including IP and application documents); provide guidance on confidentiality prior to assessors undertaking assessment; comply with relevant data protection legislation for all data received. UKRI will ensure reviewer identities are only known to UKRI administrators and kept anonymous to applicants (though panellists may know reviewer identity where necessary); instruct reviewers not to inadvertently identify themselves in assessment text and request they do not directly or indirectly discuss their involvement in reviewing with others including on social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment and funding decisions must be conducted in a responsible manner, promoting and safeguarding the public value of research and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI will make funding decisions based on evidence and rigorous analysis; provide resources for assessors and applicants on research ethics and good conduct through UKRI policy and the good research resource hub; expects assessors to understand and adhere to core values of the Concordat to Support Research Integrity and to take these into account when assessing; will ensure these core values are considered in funding decisions; provide a supportive and open environment for assessors and staff; expects all recipients of funding to work within best practices and policies relating to trusted research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment and decision-making should drive a culture of equality, diversity and inclusion, providing the best opportunities where individuals and teams of people from all backgrounds can thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UKRI’s assessment process will reduce biases against those with protected characteristics (listed: age; disability; gender reassignment; marriage and civil partnership; pregnancy and maternity; race; religion or belief; sex and sexual orientation). UKRI will conduct equality impact assessments for all new funding opportunities to identify impacts and mitigation steps; have a transparent and robust process for selecting panellists and reviewers, utilising talent from underrepresented groups; collect and make publicly available EDI data on research funding and regional distribution including quality-related research funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of duties and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment of an application must be undertaken by assessors with the appropriate expertise and who are kept clearly separate from the final funding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per the Haldane principle, funding decisions on individual applications will be made only after receiving independent assessment of their quality. Assessors may review applications and provide advice, scores, or recommendations based on their expert judgements; these contributions are advisory. Final funding and investment decisions are made solely by UKRI staff with the relevant delegated authority. UKRI staff or staff from co-funders with appropriate expertise may act as assessors, but final investment decisions must always be taken independently by UKRI decision-makers who were not involved in the assessment of the applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of policy and requirement to justify deviation
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy covers all competitive funding opportunities delivered by the seven UKRI disciplinary councils that go through an assessment process; it does not cover funding decisions made through algorithms or where there is no element of direct competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All UKRI competitive funding opportunities must demonstrate how they meet the principles in this policy, or where there is a justified reason for a different approach. Where a funding opportunity is co-funded with an external partner, UKRI will work with the partner and agree an approach that maintains the globally recognised standards encapsulated by these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles, review types and definitions (assessor, reviewer, review, panellist, panel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and expectations for roles and review types used in the assessment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding opportunity: an opportunity to submit an application to carry out research/innovation activities. Assessment: process to determine application quality based on assessment criteria (forms include review and panel). Assessment criteria: published criteria used to make funding recommendations. Assessor: evaluates individual merit against published criteria and must be able to provide appropriate and relevant assessment; can be from business, academia, non-academic bodies or the general public. Reviewer: an assessor with expertise in the relevant field to provide a detailed assessment; can provide relevant expertise on all or part of an application. Review: involves assessment independently of other applications, is based on the reviewer’s judgement of the assessment criteria alone, and does not normally benchmark against other applications. Panellist: an assessor invited to sit as a panel member with relevant experience/expertise (academia, business, public sector, charity, or general public). Panel: meeting where assessment is carried out collectively against criteria with the main aim to rank or categorise applications in priority for funding or to progress in the assessment process.
